messages:
maya: Nightly eval alert — the quantized-v2 candidate (q8->q4) is showing a high regression rate on the long-history prompt set. Lots of instruction-following failures and truncated instruction tails. Posting a couple quick examples and the nightly summary from the bot.

nightly-bot: nightly-eval: model=quantized-v2 commit=gh:alice/serve@r1842 failed=18/120 long_history_suite, avg_len=2048, latency_ok=true, severity=high. Full logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/nightly/2123456789

tony: Can you paste a short failing example? Want to see if it's prefix cut or content drop.

maya: Sure — here's one from the failing set (prompt + model generation):

```
PROMPT: "You are a helpful editor. Convert the following instruction into a concise checklist. History:
1) Please preserve the email headers.
2) Make sure to remove all PII.
3) Also, rewrite the subject to be shorter."

EXPECTED: Checklist with 3 items referencing headers, PII removal, rewrite subject.

GENERATION (quantized-v2, seed=42): "Sure.
- Remove PII
- Rewrite subject"

-> Missing: explicit instruction to preserve headers (first item dropped).
```

li-wei: Hm that's not just truncation at the end — it's selective instruction loss. Any sign of KV-cache slot wrap or seqnum misalign?

maya: I grepped the runtime logs for KV warnings. Saw a few entries around the same time: `kv_slot=-1 adjust_delta=256` and one `kv_index_wrap detected for session=xyz`.

eduardo: I ran a targeted run on my dev box reproducer with the same prompt and seed across quantization levels: q16 -> OK, q8 -> flaky, q4 -> reproducible. So it correlates with quant aggressiveness.

tony: Interesting. Could quantization change tokenization alignment or the way prefix caching is stored? Maybe low-bit kernels are dropping high-precision markers used for special tokens.

li-wei: Possible. Also check runtime change r1809 (KV slot index refactor) — I think the new index math interacts badly with reduced activations in q4. Could produce off-by-one when stitching cache.

maya: Reproducer run log (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-18T04:12:03Z] REQUEST id=abc session=xyz seq=0 pref_len=512
[2026-03-18T04:12:03Z] RUNTIME: attach_kv(session=xyz) -> base_idx=131072
[2026-03-18T04:12:03Z] RUNTIME: write_kv(slot=131072 len=64)
[2026-03-18T04:12:03Z] RUNTIME: attach_kv(session=xyz) -> base_idx=131136
[2026-03-18T04:12:03Z] RUNTIME: kv_index_wrap detected session=xyz at seq=512
[2026-03-18T04:12:03Z] MODEL q4: generate -> token 143 ("preserve") omitted context check mismatch
```

eduardo: That `kv_index_wrap` is suspicious. If the cache offset rotates mid-session and quant kernels assume different layout, we could lose tokens when reconstructing attention keys.

tony: Can we repro with a deterministic small sequence that triggers wrap? If yes, we should add an assert in runtime that checks reconstructed attention against raw activations on debug builds.

maya: I created a minimal script: `tools/repro_long_kv.py --prompt tests/long_history/keep_headers.txt --seed 42 --quant q4` and attached logs. Reproduces locally ~80% of runs.

li-wei: I'll run a bisect across runtime commits and quant kernels. Plan: (1) run repro with q8/q4 across r1780..r1850, (2) enable `--kv-debug` to dump raw attention keys, (3) push a failing trace to s3 for the model team.

nightly-bot: started job: eng-ml/kv-bisect-2123456789 (owner=li-wei). Link: https://ci.internal/redwood/bisect/2123456789

eduardo: Quick note — metric looks like instruction-drop-rate (IDR). On the nightly harness we see IDR baseline=0.6% -> quantized-v2=12.3% on long_history. Short prompts unaffected.

maya: Agreed. Action items:
- li-wei: run bisect and attach one full attention-dump trace (deadline EOD PST)
- tony: add runtime assert to debug builds to detect cache misalignment (PR today)
- eduardo: prepare fallback policy to route long_history suite to q8 while we fix (console flag)

tony: I'll open a small PR: `runtime: kv-align-assert` with opt-out via env var. Will tag you for review @li-wei @maya.

li-wei: Bisect started. First pass narrowed to r1806..r1814 where failure rate jumps. Uploading trace to s3 now.

maya: Thanks all. If bisect nails a commit, we can roll the quantized candidate back from nightly and re-run. For visibility, leaving this thread pinned to eng-ml triage. :mag: :exclamation:

eduardo: Repro artifacts: s3://redwood-dev/triage/2123456789/trace-xyz-raw-keys.tar.gz (public-internal link).

nightly-bot: job eng-ml/kv-bisect-2123456789 completed: suspect_range=r1806..r1810, repro_count=27/30, next_steps=runtime-assert + model-team-verify

maya: Great. We'll follow up with an RCA once we have the assert failure trace. Thanks everyone.

tony: :thumbsup:
